source.citation: Kurz & Allison. Chicago In Early Days, 1779-1857. Chicago: Kurz & Allison, 76 & 78 Wabash Avenue, 1893. Chromolithograph, fifteen numbered vignettes with printed key.
what_it_does_not_supply: any coordinate, footprint outline or dimension — tier 5, and a perspective vignette cannot be asked for a metre
a date for anything it draws that can be relied on: its own key puts the Kinzie Mansion at 1832, which contradicts every documentary source this project holds
independent testimony for panel 14, which follows the F. Braunhold engraving in Andreas (1884) closely enough to be probably derived from it
any evidence that a garden fence stood on a lot in the town: panel 12 is the north bank, and the house it draws is excluded from the 1835 scene (data/exclusions.json, kinzie_house)
a height, a pale width or a bay for the fence it draws — every dimension on the fence layer is invented, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L129 says so
a Lombardy poplar anywhere in Chicago but this one group
a view of the 1835 fort in panel 8: that panel is dated 1830 by the sheet's own key and was mistaken for a fort plate for a month (T-1107)
what_it_supplies: panel 1: Old Fort Dearborn of 1803 from across the river - the palisade under a ruled cap line, the barracks ranges, the blockhouses and the bare trodden ground outside the walls that data/enclosures/fort_dearborn_apron.json is built on

panel 8: the town from the lake in 1830, population 96 - the low far bank, a lodge and bark canoes on the shore, and trees round the buildings on both banks; a scene-adjacent TOWN view, five years early, not a second view of the fort
panel 12: the long low Kinzie house with a full-width piazza on its front, a red roof, and outbuildings up the rise behind it
panel 12: a row of four Lombardy poplars standing between the house and the river — the count and rhythm tools/generate_planted_rows.py measures across seven plates
panel 12: PICKET-FENCED garden plots at the house — close-set vertical pales, the treatment data/enclosures/town_dooryard_pickets.json deals to the town's house lots
panel 12: the fenced green between house and water that Wau-Bun describes in words, drawn
panel 11: the Green Tree Hotel as a two-storey clapboard block with end chimneys and even sash, with ship masts behind it
panel 5: Fort Dearborn as rebuilt 1835 — picket palisade, galleried barracks range, blockhouse
panel 14: the Sauganash Hotel as a two-storey clapboard block with an attached single-storey log wing and no full-width gallery
the sheet's printed key, which names each panel and dates several of the buildings
